is down ~22% in after-hours trading Thursday after saying that it has paused enrollment in studies of azetukalner for major depressive disorder and bipolar depression following neuropsychiatric adverse events.

"The observed events, the rate of these events and their severity, are consistent with the known safety and tolerability profile of azetukalner and its mechanism; however, such adverse events had not previously been seen in the Phase 2 X‑NOVA clinical study in MDD," the company said in a news release.
Patients currently enrolled and those in open-label extension studies will continue in the study.
Xenon said it expects the pause to be temporary and is working on dosing adjustments to lower the adverse events.
The pause does not impact studies of azetukalner in focal seizures and primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
an NDA to the US FDA for azetukalner in focal seizures.

title: Xenon drops after pausing enrollment in azetukalner studies for depression
